I'm heartbroken as my dad passed away late last night. But, after some thought, I can still find 1. Dad is at peace now and for that I am grateful. 2. I got to spend these last years with him under my roof, creating memories I’ll hold onto forever. 3. Love doesn’t end here—the love he gave continues to shape me, even in the hardest moments. Bonus: I’m holding close the memory of our last real vacation together at what used to be my grandparent's cabin on Lake Superior — and this photo reminds me that even in grief, there is still beauty to look toward.

40 Mile Point Lighthouse The 40 Mile Point Lighthouse was authorized by congress in 1893. The lighthouse gets its name from being 40 miles south of Mackinaw Point on Lake Huron. The lighthouse was completed at the end of 1896 but wasn't lit until it was manned and ready during the spring of the following year. The light was put on the National Register of Historical places in 1984.

Cheboygan Crib The Cheboygan Crib Lighthouse is owned and operated by the Great Lakes Lighthouse Keepers. This lighthouse sits at the mouth of the Cheboygan River and Lake Huron in what is now Gordon Turner Park. Originally built in 1884 the crib has gone through a number of renovations. The original building was made of wood and replaced with concrete in 1903.

The Iroquois Point Lighthouse began service on September 20, 1857, over one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, located at the entrance to the St. Mary's River on Lake Superior. After 107 years, it was replaced by an automatic light off Gros Cap, Ontario, in 1964. The lighthouse was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1975.

I heard the news on TV and read the newspapers when it happened. Pictures I took myself of the ruined lifeboat (found empty) on display at the Valley Camp Museum in Sault Ste Marie, the actual ship's bell from the Fitzgerald at the Great Lakes Shipwreck Museum in Whitefish Point. The Dossin Great Lakes Museum on Belle Isle here in Detroit has preserved the wheelhouse of the William Clay Ford which (with the Arthur Anderson) was sent out to look for the Fitzgerald while it was still storming. Feels a bit weird to stand in it and think about that night. I've also attended a memorial service for the Fitz at Old Mariners Church in Detroit and read a couple of books on the subject. Oh yeah, I have the original Gordon Lightfoot album (on vinyl, no less) that contained the song.
